sources.name: ArchDaily
sources.summary: Steven Holl Architects has been selected to lead the renewal of Ida Noyes Hall at the University of Chicago in Illinois . The project will upgrade the 111-year-old building's infrastructure, improve accessibility , and introduce new spaces for programs, events, and informal gathering while preserving its historic character. Designed by Shepley, Rutan & Coolidge and completed in 1916, Ida Noyes Hall was originally conceived as a women's clubhouse and has since evolved into a broader campus gathering space. JLK Architects will serve as the historic preservation architect, with Workshop Architects leading student-life programming and operations planning.
